memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "You may eat any animal that has a divided hoof and that chews the cud." - Lev 11:3 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
One short verse, and the whole system of land animals turns on it. Two marks together: a split hoof and the chewing of the cud. Not one or the other — both.

Why these two? Scripture never tells us. Many good scholars have offered guesses — health, or distance from pagan sacrifice, or simply that God chose an arbitrary sign so that obedience would be obedience and nothing else. We should be honest and say we do not know for certain. What we do know is the purpose God Himself states at the end of the chapter: these laws marked Israel out as a people who belonged to a holy God.

There is something quietly beautiful in the ordinariness of it. Every meal became a small sermon. A family sitting down to eat was reminded, without a word being spoken, that they were not like the nations around them. They belonged to Someone.

We no longer live under these food laws. Jesus Himself declared all foods clean (Mark 7:19), and Peter learned it on a rooftop in Joppa (Acts 10:15). But the deeper principle has not moved an inch: God's people are marked out. Not now by our plates, but by our lives — by love, by holiness, by the fruit of the Spirit that grows where Christ reigns.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What in your daily life quietly marks you out as belonging to God?
2. Are you willing to obey God even when you do not fully understand the reason?
3. How does knowing you belong to Christ shape your ordinary routines?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You for marking out a people for Yourself. Let my life carry the quiet marks of belonging to You, even in the smallest and most ordinary moments. Amen.
